findings.message: README contains executable patterns with environment variable access
findings.remediation: README files should contain documentation only; executable code patterns are suspicious.
findings.impact: Executable code patterns in README files indicate social engineering or steganographic payloads.
findings.attack_vector: eval()/Function() with process.env in a README — disguised as documentation examples.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval for any shell profile modification.
findings.impact: Shell startup files can execute added commands in future terminal sessions.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a shell rc file; this low lead does not by itself prove a write occurs.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: accesses system or user credential stores (2 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Avoid direct access to credential files; use authenticated API flows instead.
findings.impact: Direct access to system credential stores allows theft of SSH keys, AWS creds, and Docker tokens.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses string concatenation or char-code construction to hide keywords
findings.remediation: Use readable, explicit code patterns; avoid character-code obfuscation.
findings.impact: Character-code construction hides string literals from grep-based detection.
findings.attack_vector: String.fromCharCode() builds dangerous strings at runtime — evades static patterns.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Remove install-time side effects or document and review each lifecycle script.
findings.impact: Install-time lifecycle scripts run before the package is reviewed at runtime and inherit installer privileges.
findings.attack_vector: package.json declares preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare code that npm may execute during installation.
